significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) ordering—behavioral coupling is "stronger for languages where honorifics are grammatically obligatory"—combined with a form-(ii) mechanism in which a largely shared, causal "status direction" changes sycophancy, hedging, and refusal and leaks into another output language. This establishes both a phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing predictions across several behaviors and language classes rather than merely showing decodability; this bears directly on the user-opinion dependence studied in Perez et al. (2022) and Sharma et al. (2023), and on shared multilingual processing implicated by Wendler et al. (2024). Verified false, the conjunction would rule out grammaticalized status as a shared causal explanation of these behaviors and favor language-specific or behaviorally inert encoding, so the branches are distinguishable and informative despite possible mixed component outcomes. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit: deleting the obligatoriness gradient, cross-language leakage, and multi-behavior causal coupling leaves only the generic multilingual-representation topic, which would not justify this score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "status direction," a prompt-time status probe, and the proposed ability to "ablate the direction to REMOVE honorific-induced sycophancy"; the probe and intervention are ex ante because they can flag or alter status conditioning before the answer and its agreement error are produced. Although the direction would require re-extraction per model, the substantive conclusion predicts what recalibration should reveal: stronger status–behavior coupling in obligatory-honorific languages and leakage from honorific prompts into answers in another language. The asserted scope spans "typologically diverse honorific languages," non-honorific comparison languages, and multilingual models, and the downstream users could include model auditors and deployers seeking to detect or suppress socially conditioned compliance, though the conclusion does not itself travel outside AI. The topic-substitution check confirms that this reach comes from the specific transferable relation and preventive handle, not merely from studying multilingual models.
